newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium's Solvay sells unit, to spend in U.S.
newsitem.headline: Belgium's Solvay sells unit, to spend in U.S.

text.p: Belgian chemicals group Solvay S.A. said Friday it would sell its worldwide animal health businesses to American Home Products Corp. for 14 billion Belgian francs ($449 million).
Solvay said its sale of the unit to the Madison, N.J.-based drug and health care products company will net it a pre-tax capital gain of around six billion francs ($192 million).
With a large credit line renewed with a number of European banks last month, the group has reserves of about $1 billion at its disposal.
Solvay said it plans to acquire human pharmaceutical product lines or companies in the United States.
"We are not looking, except if an extraordinary opportunity arises, for one mega-acquisition," said Daniel Janssen, Solvay's chief executive officer, at a news conference.
"For the moment we are working on selective acquisitions ... in therapeutic areas where we are strong," he said.
Janssen noted Solvay's share of the pharmaceuticals market in Europe was more than 1 percent in 1995 but only 0.3 percent in the United States. "We want to grow much faster in the U.S," he said.

Janssen said Solvay had already made some unannounced U.S. acquisitions this year and would continue to investigate opportunites as they arose. "But don't expect by the end of the year to see anything spectacular," he said.
Juergen Ernst, director of Solvay's health business, said the company, which has the world's 44th largest drug business in 1995, was also concentrating on new products and markets.
Solvay human health sales overall amounted to 34 billion Belgian francs ($1.1 billion) in 1995 out of total group sales of 273 billion francs ($8.8 billion).
Americna Home Products stock was up 25 cents at $63 a share in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
